newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French consumption falls in Sept.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French consumption falls in Sept.

text.p: The following are economists' comments on a fall of 1.5 percent in French consumer spending on manufactured goods in September.
"It's disappointing. Taking into account the August revision higher it's still slightly disappointing.
Nevertheless the third quarter was up 2.5 percent from the second quarter on a non-annualised basis which is consistent with the overall very strong consumption in the third quarter.
But car sales will drop and the fourth quarter will be extremely disappointing.
PHILIPPE BROSSARD, HEAD OF RESEARCH, ABN AMRO, PARIS

It is a disappointing figure. The August revision compensates a little, but not completely. I was looking for a rise (in September) of as much as three percent. Last time we also had big car sales but there had already been a big drop in shoes and other items which we thought would not be reproduced.

It shows that growth is a little less than expected because to pay for all these car sales people are cutting down on other spending. For the third quarter it might take 0.1 pct or 0.2 percent off GDP growth to around 0.8 or 0.9 percent.
However, it may limit the fallback in October when car sales stop and people start spending on other goods which have been low for two months now.

It is not a surprise since we knew hypermarket sales were down. Now we will have a fairly moderate fourth quarter. There is no rise in purchasing power. If people have bought cars they have bought them with their savings, and they are not going to buy other things this year.
HERVE GOULLETQUER, ECONOMIST, CAISSE CENTRALE DES BANQUES POPULAIRES

Given the steep fall in hypermarket sales announced at the start of the month, it was to be expected. I was even expecting worse for consumer spending. Over the whole of the third quarter, consumption has been fairly strong with a 2.6 percent rise. Overall I am maintaining my forecast for GDP growth of one percent for the third quarter, while the fourth quarter is likely, however, to be less good.
SONJA GIBBS, BOND ANALYST, NOMURA INTERNATIONAL
What a shocker. It's very supportive of PIBOR and hopes for a rate cut next week. Most people had expected a very strong number.
In the absence of auto sales one would have probably expected a pull back in September anyway.
It highlights that France remains weak compared to Germany.
